findings.title: Duplicate definition of self.downsize shadows the width/height variant and breaks its call signature
findings.body: The file now defines `self.downsize` twice (lines 145 and 149). In Ruby the second definition silently replaces the first, so the four-argument version `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` is dead code. Worse, any existing caller invoking the old 4-argument form `downsize(from, to, w, h)` now hits the new signature `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`, which binds `dimensions = w` and `opts = h` (an Integer). `optimize` then calls `opts[:allow_animation]` on an Integer and raises, and the dimensions string becomes just the width with no height. Either delete the old definition or rename/reorder so both signatures work.

findings.title: Downsizing runs ImageMagick in-place on the uploaded tempfile, corrupting or mis-formatting the image
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` passes the same path as both the convert input and output, and that path is a Rack multipart tempfile with no file extension. ImageMagick's `convert` is documented as unsafe for reading and writing the same file (it can truncate/corrupt the source when pixels are cached to disk for large images), and writing to a filename with no recognized suffix makes ImageMagick default to an unexpected format (typically MIFF) rather than PNG/JPEG. The result can be a corrupted or wrongly-formatted file that is then stored as the upload under the original filename/extension. The downsize should write to a second tempfile (with a matching extension) and the result should replace the original only after a successful conversion.

findings.title: Client-side upload size limits hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site settings
findings.body: The check previously used `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, so admins could configure separate `max_image_size_kb` and `max_attachment_size_kb`. It is now hardcoded to 10MB for both images and attachments. Consequences: (1) on sites with a limit below 10MB, users are no longer warned client-side and uploads up to 10MB are submitted only to be rejected server-side; (2) on sites with a limit above 10MB, valid uploads are now blocked in the browser; (3) attachments have no relation to the new server-side image downsizing, yet their limit was also changed. If the intent was only to relax the client check for images (since the server now downsizes them), the attachment path should still honor `max_attachment_size_kb`.

findings.title: 413 error handler reports a hardcoded 10MB limit that may not match the server
findings.body: The 413 branch previously read `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to tell the user the actual server limit; it now always says 10MB. If the web server rejects at a different threshold (nginx `client_max_body_size` or a site setting above/below 10MB), the user gets a wrong limit in the error message and will keep retrying files that can never succeed, or wrongly believe larger files are allowed.

findings.title: API URL download limit hardcoded to 10MB, bypassing and capping the site setting
findings.body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. This breaks in both directions: a site that configured a smaller `max_image_size_kb` now has API users downloading arbitrarily larger remote files (which are then run through up to five ImageMagick conversions, a CPU cost), and a site that configured a limit above 10MB can no longer pull images larger than 10MB via the API. The download cap should be a fixed ceiling (e.g. `MAX_IMAGE_SIZE` constant larger than any allowed setting) or remain derived from the setting, not an unexplained magic 10MB that silently diverges from configuration.

findings.title: Downsize loop ignores conversion failures and may loop on a corrupted file
findings.body: The `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > ...` loop never checks the return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize`, which returns false when the convert command fails. If conversion fails (e.g. unsupported/corrupt image, or the in-place issue noted separately), the code runs the same failing conversion four more times and then passes the possibly truncated/unchanged file to `Upload.create_for`. Each failed iteration also invokes `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!` inside `convert_with`, multiplying wasted CPU. The loop should break out immediately when `downsize` returns false and surface an error to the user.

findings.title: Animated-GIF branch can never trigger for uploaded files, flattening animated images to one frame
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.optimize` selects the animated (gifsicle) code path only when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but the path passed here is the uploaded Rack tempfile, which never ends in `.gif`. So for an animated GIF upload, `convert` is used with `#{from}[0]`, which takes only the first frame: the stored upload silently loses its animation even when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is enabled. The animation check needs to work off the filename/extension of the upload, not the tempfile path (or the tempfile should be created with the original extension).

findings.title: Up to five sequential convert + ImageOptim passes on 10MB images in the request/defer path
findings.body: Each downsize attempt runs a full ImageMagick convert plus an `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!` pass on a file that can now be up to 10MB (previously capped at `max_image_size_kb`). In the async path this happens inside `Scheduler::Defer.later`, and in the synchronous API path it happens inline in the request, blocking a web worker for potentially tens of seconds. Five iterations of 80% only reduce to ~33% of the original, so a badly compressible image will do all five passes. Consider a single conversion computed from the target size, and skip ImageOptim on intermediate passes.

findings.title: No tests for the new automatic downsizing behavior
findings.body: The PR adds a meaningful behavior change (oversized images being silently resized on upload, animated handling, the 5-attempt loop) but includes no controller or model tests covering it: e.g. an image above `max_image_size_kb` gets downsized and accepted, a non-image file above the limit is still rejected, a failed conversion does not produce a corrupt upload, and an animated GIF preserves animation when allowed. Given the in-place and format-detection pitfalls above, this code path needs coverage before merge.
